the PVdF morphology plays a significant role in determining the electrochemical performance of the solid-state electrolyte.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PVdF morphology has a significant effect on the LiFSi/[C2mpyl][FSI] phase and electrochemical performance, and the best results are obtained using the PVdF nanofibers.

, although the addition of PVdF does not improve the performance of the 50 wt% LiFSI/[EMIm][FSI] composite electrolyte in Li metal batteries, the PVdFs used in this work can improve the stability of Li metal batteries with a 50 wt.% LiFSI/[ C2mpyr][ FSI] solid electrolyte.

The main takeaway from our work is that

, while the addition of PVdF to the electrolyte mix is beneficial, it can also lead to undesired effects such as the formation of an amorphous phase, which can be detrimental to the electrochemical performance.

the morphology and concentration of PVdF in an OIPC electrolyte has a significant effect on the phase behavior, and thus the electrochemical performance of a Li metal battery cell using this type of electrolyte.
the addition of PVdF to the OIPC electrolyte can be used to tune the phase behavior and the resulting electrochemical stability.
